Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

lexio 1.0.1

  • The package and the database of the thesis are archived on Zenodo, with DOIs: the package, all versions, 10.5281/zenodo.24293765; the database, 10.5281/zenodo.24293808. They are now in citation("lexio"), CITATION.cff and the README.
  • Replication: when replication/thesis_data is missing, the scripts download the database from the GitHub release and, if that fails, from its Zenodo record; the SHA-256 of the file is checked in both cases.

lexio 1.0.0

First public release.

  • declare_io() declares an input-output database from objects already in R: the technical structure (Z, A or B), gross output, final demand, any number of satellite accounts (levels E or coefficients D) and, optionally, a corridor on the economic deviations (corridor, or floor and ceiling). read_io() reads the same database from CSV files (including those saved by Excel as “CSV UTF-8”) or an .xlsx workbook; write_io(), validate_io(), example_io() and lexio_template() complete the set.
  • define_model() and read_model() declare the direction and goal of each account (base, growth, pooled_share, delta, level), the economic block (fixed at the last level unless declared free; absolute or relative deviations), the scenarios, the corridor and the priorities: all k! orderings, permutations of groups, or explicit orderings with several weighted goals per level.
  • run_model() runs every ordering of every scenario; run_experiment() runs one. Each priority level is a linear program solved with GLPK, with the optima of the earlier levels locked. lock_tolerance = "auto" solves again, with a slightly relaxed lock, only the runs where GLPK reports a level as not optimal, and flags them. A level that GLPK does not certify is checked against its constraints: if they hold, the numbers are kept and the run is flagged; if not, the level has no solution, and it and the following levels are left blank.
  • write_outputs() writes a report, CSV tables of every level of every run and an Excel workbook; write_excel() writes the workbook alone.
  • Vignettes: getting started, declaring data and models, the goal programming example of Miller and Blair, and the replication of the thesis. Portuguese translations are on the package website.
